messages:
samira: Heads-up — onboarding demo with the local dev-tunnel (ngrok) produced duplicate invoice callbacks. Two POSTs for inv_777 ~150ms apart.
eli: logs or repro?
samira: pasted minimal trace from the sampleapp wrapper: 
```
2026-04-10T14:05:12.001Z WARN retry: status=429 attempt=1 req=inv_777
2026-04-10T14:05:12.152Z INFO retry: backoff_ms=0 jitter_ms=0 seed=0x2a
2026-04-10T14:05:12.152Z INFO sender: POST /callbacks inv_777 idempotency=absent
2026-04-10T14:05:12.303Z INFO sender: POST /callbacks inv_777 idempotency=absent
```
samira: context: sampleapp runs under our dev-tunnel which forks worker processes to attach to multiple ngrok tunnels for each dev. Rust SDK's RNG state was seeded once in the parent; children inherited identical RNG state and produced the same jitter sequence.
tara: ah, fork + rng inheritance. we saw similar in C world but didn't expect it in our Rust sampleapp. which SDKs are affected?
samira: Rust and Ruby builds seed PRNG at startup and don't reseed after fork. Node/Python call a fresh RNG per thread so they were okay in this repro.
kevin: why was idempotency absent? sampleapp CLI sets SAFE_REPLAY=false in quickstart to keep payloads "clean" in demos. that was a mistake.
eli: so root cause = forked processes inheriting RNG -> synchronized retries + sampleapp disabling Idempotency-Key -> duplicate side-effect. combo perfecto.
tara: fix ideas:
- SDK: add explicit "reseed_on_fork" hook or call thread_rng().seed_from_u64(Crypto::random()) in any child process after fork; docs note for Rust/Ruby.
- Sampleapp: change quickstart default SAFE_REPLAY -> true; simplify demo logs instead via a verbose flag not by disabling safe replay.
- Dev-tunnel: provide a --single-process option to avoid forking by default for onboarding demos.
- Add a tiny jitter floor (1-4ms) even in "deterministic" dev modes unless user passes --zero-jitter-explicit.
- Add an automated CI check that runs the dev-tunnel fork scenario on a small VM and asserts no duplicate callbacks.
kevin: also, SDK parity: ensure Rust/Ruby/Go all provide a clear after_fork reseed API and document the risk in onboarding.
samira: small UX idea: emit a runtime warning if process detects it was forked (pid != parent_pid_at_seed) and deterministic retries are enabled: "Detected fork after RNG seed: this may synchronize retries across replicas and cause duplicated side-effects. See docs."
eli: agree. testers: we should add an integration test that simulates NGROK-style multiple tunnels by spawning N child processes within a second and exercising retries to ensure at most one POST for the same idempotency key.
build-bot: created PR 4977: rust-sdk -> reseed_on_fork + tiny jitter floor. CI queued.
ops-bot: ticket INF-3187 created: "dev-tunnel forked workers inherit RNG -> duplicate callbacks" assigned to @kevin.
kevin: action items:@samira - add repro script and update sampleapp quickstart to enable SAFE_REPLAY by default and add --single-process flag; @tara - doc changes and SDK parity note; @eli - test harness in CI; @kevin - verify PR and release patch.
samira: thanks team. temp mitigation for customers: run sampleapp with `--single-process` or set SAFE_REPLAY=1. Also avoid dev-tunnel for multi-replica demos until we release the patch.
eli: will add a line to onboarding checklist: "do not fork processes without reseeding RNG or enabling safe replay".
kevin: PR 4977 merged to staging. smoke tests green. will push to main after 24h of monitoring.
samira: resolving for now, will reopen if we see any more duplicates in customer demos.
